critical.issue: Setting is_default=true on a non-default market returns 500 Internal Server Error from Postgres unique constraint 'uq_tenant_markets_default' (Key (tenant_id) already exists). Root cause in /app/backend/routers/markets.py patch_my_tenant_market: lines 195-209 upsert the target row FIRST (with is_default=true), THEN at lines 211-214 clear other tenants_markets defaults. The upsert hits the unique constraint before the clear-others runs. Fix: clear-others BEFORE the upsert (move the 'enforce mutex' block to run before insert/update), OR wrap both ops in a transaction and clear first.

integration_issues.issue: End-to-end Set-as-default + Save flow fails silently from the user's POV because the underlying PATCH /tenants/me/markets/{usa_id} {is_default:true} returns 500. The frontend shows 'Salvataggio fallito' (Save failed) toast. UI logic is correct — bug is the backend mutex order.

rca_of_the_issue: Postgres unique constraint uq_tenant_markets_default(tenant_id) WHERE is_default=true exists to enforce single default. The patch endpoint upserts the target row with is_default=true FIRST (line 196 update / line 209 insert), which violates the constraint because the previous default (Italy) is still is_default=true at that moment. The intended mutex clear at lines 212-214 runs AFTER and is unreachable when the constraint fires. Reproduction: PATCH /api/tenants/me/markets/{usa_id} {is_default:true,is_active:true} → 500. Mitigation: re-order — clear others first, then upsert. Better: wrap in a transaction or use a single SQL CTE / RPC.
